newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Private companies seek expansion of Paranagua port.
newsitem.headline: Private companies seek expansion of Paranagua port.

text.p: Private companies with facilities at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua are planning a series of investments to increase grain loading capacity to 30 million tonnes a year from seven million, a cooperative said.

"We are already working on an agreement with the state government...to increase loading capacity at the port from seven to 30 million tonnes annually," said Jose Aroldo Gallassini, president of Cooperativa Agropecuaria Mouraoense (Coamo).
Paranagua loaded a combined total of 8.63 million tonnes of soybeans and soymeal in 1996, as well as 804,139 tonnes of vegetable oils, including soyoil.

In the year to July 20, the port loaded 3.45 million tonnes of soybeans, up from 1.52 million tonnes in the same period last year. It loaded 3.34 million tonnes of soymeal, compared with 3.85 million at the same time in 1996.
Corn loading totalled 248,437 tonnes by July 20, up from 93,928 tonnes last year.

The port has been expanding since the implementation of a Brazil-wide port modernization law and on Friday published details of the privatization tender of various facilities, including its container terminal and export corridor.
The port authority expect the sell-off to take place by the end of the year.

As part of the modernization, private companies are aiming to increase grain loading to 1,500 tonnes per hour at the port's four shiploaders, compared to the current average of 602 tonnes per hour, Gallassini said.
"The agreement would be that loading could never fall below 1,000 tonnes per hour," he said. "The great drama at Paranagua was the waiting of ships and the large fines that there were."

Soybean traders said long queues were common at Paranagua in 1996, with vessels waiting up to 35 days for product. The situation eased somewhat this year after the port introduced 24-hour loading at its export corridor.

Coamo, the largest cooperative in Brazil with 19,000 members, plans to invest 27 million reais ($25 million) in increasing its loading capacity, expanding its warehouse space and increasing its soyoil crushing capacity at the port.
The cooperative will add 40,000 tonnes warehousing capacity to its existing 42,000-tonne space, Gallassini said. In addition, Coamo will double its soyoil processing capacity to 2,000 tonnes per day.
Gallassini said private firms at the port, including Cargill, Cotriguacu and Coinbra, had been negotiating a joint investment program with the Parana state government over the last two years.
The plan calls for the state to invest nine to 10 million reais and private firms some 15 million reais to increase the port's capacity, he said.
But the port authority said nothing had been finalized yet and it had no knowledge of the expansion plans.

Coamo last week approved a series of investments at its industrial plant in Campo Mourao, including a 4.3 million reais budget for the construction of a margarine factory forecast to produce 60 tonnes per day as of late 1998.

The cooperative also plans to build a wheat mill with a capacity of 200 tonnes per day, at a cost of just under five million reais, and to expand its existing hydrous alcohol factory to start producing anhydrous alcohol.

Coamo's production includes soybeans, coffee, corn, wheat, rice, beans and cotton and it registered profits of $809 million in 1996, of which soybeans accounted for 30 percent. The cooperative forecast profits of $850 million in 1997.
Coamo loaded some 600,000 tonnes of grains at Paranagua in 1996 -- mostly soybeans and corn -- but this should rise to 850,000 tonnes in 1997, Gallassini said.
